newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico taps army general to head anti-drug unit.
newsitem.headline: Mexico taps army general to head anti-drug unit.

text.p: A Mexican army general and member of the elite presidential guard has been appointed to head the country's leading drug-fighting agency, officials said on Tuesday.

General Jose Gutierrez Rebollo replaces Francisco Javier Molina Ruiz as head of the National Anti-Drug Institute, according to a spokesman at the attorney general's office, which oversees national drug fighting efforts.

Molina Ruiz was fired on Monday by President Ernesto Zedillo as part of a larger shake up within the attorney general's office. Zedillo also replaced Attorney General Antonio Lozano with ex-human rights ombudsman Jorge Madrazo Cuellar.
Madrazo late on Monday named Ismael Eslava Perez as special prosecutor to investigate the 1994 killing of ruling party secretary general Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu.
Raul Salinas, brother of ex-president Carlos Salinas, is currently in jail charged with masterminding that killing.

Eslava replaced Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, a prosecutor who resigned following Lozano's ouster. Chapa was also recently taken off the case of another high profile assassination after he was unable to jail any of his suspects.
